articles.headline: Panthers scratch LB Devin Lloyd; WRs Coker, Legette questionable
articles.description: The Panthers will be without starting linebacker Devin Lloyd (calf) against the Browns, while wide receivers Jalen Coker (ankle) and Xavier Legette (knee) have been listed as questionable.
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers will be without starting linebacker Devin Lloyd against the Cleveland Browns, as the reigning NFC Defensive Player of the Week has been ruled out with a calf injury.

Wide receivers Jalen Coker (ankle) and Xavier Legette (knee) are listed as questionable. Panthers coach Dave Canales said he expects Coker to play against the Browns, but Legette will be a game-time decision.

Lloyd is coming off one of the more impressive showings by a linebacker in the past decade. In the 34-3 win over the Atlanta Falcons, Lloyd produced nine total tackles, a sack, three pass breakups, two interceptions and a defensive touchdown. He did not practice this week.

The Panthers will rely on fellow starter Bobby Okereke to lead the defense with recently promoted veteran Tyrel Dodson seeing his first action of the season. Carolina also has rookie Jackson Kuwatch, a 2026 seventh-round pick, on the roster. Claudin Cherelus, a longtime special teams ace, was ruled out Friday with a shoulder injury. The team could elevate newly re-signed linebacker/special teams ace Maema Njongmeta from the practice squad to replace Cherelus on the depth chart.

Coker leads the Panthers with 204 receiving yards and two touchdowns through two games. He sustained his ankle injury in the first quarter of Week 1's loss to the Chicago Bears, but he hasn't missed any time. He was a limited participant in practice Wednesday, didn't practice Thursday and was limited again Friday.

Legette is coming off his best performance in quite some time. He caught two passes for 64 yards against the Falcons, including a 55-yard snag that set up a touchdown score before halftime. Legette practiced Wednesday but was held out of Thursday's workout. He participated in a limited capacity Friday.

Along with Lloyd and Cherelus, safety Nick Scott (rib) was ruled out for Sunday's matchup against Cleveland. Scott is expected to be replaced by Lathan Ransom, a 2025 fourth-round pick, and Zakee Wheatley, a 2026 fifth-round pick. Wheatley forced a fumble on his first career play from scrimmage last week against the Falcons.

Outside linebacker Patrick Jones II, who missed the first two games with a back injury, will make his season debut against the Browns after being left off the final injury report.

articles.headline: Nick Chubb retires with Browns ahead of game-day honor
articles.description: Nick Chubb returned to Cleveland to officially retire as a member of the Browns, calling it "better closure" after his exit following the 2024 season.
articles.body:
BEREA, Ohio -- Four-time Pro Bowl running back Nick Chubb returned to Cleveland on Friday to officially retire as a member of the Browns, saying it was a better moment than his initial exit two seasons ago.

Chubb, 30, announced his retirement in August after eight NFL seasons, the first seven of which were spent with the Browns. A reserved but revered player who earned the respect of his teammates, coaches and opponents through his work ethic and dedication, Chubb will be honored during the Browns' home opener Sunday.

"It's great to be back. Cleveland is where my journey started, and this is where it's going to end today," Chubb said during a news conference.

The No. 35 overall pick of the 2018 draft out of Georgia, Chubb rushed for 7,349 yards and 54 touchdowns during his NFL career. He rushed for more than 1,000 yards in four straight seasons starting in 2019, including a career-high 1,525 in 2022.

A severe left knee injury in Week 2 of the 2023 season against the Pittsburgh Steelers derailed Chubb's career. He was sidelined for the final 15 games of the 2023 season and the first six games of 2024.

Chubb returned to play eight games in 2024, but his tenure in Cleveland ended with a season-ending foot injury in Week 15. The Browns did not re-sign Chubb.

"It was just kind of a sad ending," Chubb said of his time in Cleveland. "I think now it's better closure for everyone just to see me finally back in the stadium and to be in high spirits, be up and walking and moving and just for me to be back in Cleveland.

"[The injury is] something I had to come to terms with, obviously," Chubb added. "Not how I wanted it to end for me, but it happened and that's all I can do is just accept that it happened and move forward. ... I don't think that injury really sums up my career."

Chubb played his final season with the Houston Texans in 2025, rushing for 506 yards and three touchdowns.

"One, I wasn't playing for Cleveland anymore, so I didn't feel like playing football," Chubb said of his decision to retire. "But it was just a time that I thought I pretty much had done all that I could."

Chubb ranks third in Browns history in rushing yards (6,843), trailing only Jim Brown (12,312) and Leroy Kelly (7,274). Over his first five NFL seasons (2018-22), he led all running backs in yards per rush (5.2) and ranked second to Derrick Henry in rushing yards (6,341) and rushing touchdowns (48).

He said his fondest memory with the Browns will be upsetting the Steelers on the road in the wild-card round of the 2020 season.

"It was great to beat Pittsburgh in the playoffs," Chubb said. "I think that whole COVID year was a mess, but that season was really fun to me. I think just that season as a whole was just probably my favorite memory."

articles.headline: Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained
articles.description: The sporting world is waiting for a resolution to the hearings on Man City's charges for allegedly breaching the Premier League's financial rules. Here's what we know, and what might come next.
articles.body:
Editor's Note: This was originally published on March 19, 2025. We have republished and updated this explainer of the facts -- the charges levied against Manchester City, potential punishments and also insight as to the duration of the proceedings -- in light of Friday's news, which City are denying at this time. This is another helpful explainer, from Feb. 2026, shining light on why this process has taken/is taking so long.

 

What are the charges against Manchester City?

They relate to the seasons between 2009-10 and 2022-23 and cover a range of alleged breaches -- the most serious being false accounting, with respect to providing accurate financial information with respect to revenue (including sponsorship revenue), related parties and operating costs. There are other alleged breaches, including some to irregularities in player and manager remuneration and, in more recent seasons, failure to cooperate with the Premier League's investigation.

If the charges relate to alleged breaches, why are they only coming to light now?

Because much of this issue relates to the "Football Leaks," when internal documents -- "leaked" say the perpetrators, "stolen or false" say some of the victims -- relating to a range of football-related issues were made public. German newsmagazine Der Spiegel had access to the cache of documents -- including internal emails -- and published stories accusing Manchester City of flouting financial fair play rules, which regulate how clubs can generate revenue. This led to investigations by UEFA and, later, by the Premier League.

In February 2020, UEFA's investigation found Manchester City guilty and banned them from European football for two seasons while fining them €30 million. The ban was overturned five months later by the Court of Arbitration for Sport, on the basis that some charges had exceeded the statute of limitations and others were "not established" by UEFA. City were also fined €10m for failing to cooperate with the investigation.

Why is the Premier League's case taking so long?

It's a combination of the league's own rules and the many legal challenges City have brought over the years, challenging jurisdiction and other legal matters. Consider that they only announced the investigation in March 2019, then went years without telling anyone what was going on or even if the case was dropped. (In fact, it was Her Majesty's Court of Appeals that informed us in 2021 that it was still ongoing, following another legal challenge.)

By the time the charges were brought, in February 2023, nearly 4½ years had passed. And the hearing itself didn't begin until Sept. 16, 2024, some 19 months later. That hearing lasted 12 weeks, until Dec. 6 of last year. articles.headline: Sources: Giants' Jaxson Dart scheduled for left knee surgery Friday
articles.description: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is scheduled to undergo surgery Friday on his left knee, sources told ESPN. The belief is it will be a meniscus and MCL repair.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is scheduled to have surgery Friday on his left knee, sources told ESPN. The belief is it will be a meniscus and MCL repair.

Dart was injured in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Coach John Harbaugh said Dart will be out for the "regular season," leaving open the possibility he could return some time in the postseason.

It was an optimistic outlook from the Giants' coach. The Super Bowl is in four-plus months. Dart opted for a quick surgery so he can begin his rehabilitation.

The young quarterback was injured when he was sandwiched by a pair of Rams defenders on the seventh snap Monday night. He was hit on his right side by Rams linebacker Byron Young. That sent Dart into linebacker Josaiah Stewart, who slammed into the side of the quarterback's knee.

The medical personnel originally thought it was a sprained MCL, but imaging showed more severe damage the following day. Dart had tears to his MCL and meniscus, along with damage to the PCL in his left knee, sources told ESPN. His ACL remained intact.

"It sucked," running back Cam Skattebo said. "I talked to him on the sidelines a little bit, and he's my best friend. So, it's a little emotional for me. It sucked to lose him."

Dart was officially placed on injured reserve Thursday. Jameis Winston will start in his place on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. Winston completed 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and an interception in three-plus quarters against the Rams.

Dart was in team meetings and limping around the Giants facility earlier this week. He wanted to remain around the team.

"I think he's determined," Harbaugh said. "He's bummed. It's hard. The season's not over, but it is for him."

Dart, 23, flashed promise as a rookie last year and was outstanding in New York's season-opening victory over the Dallas Cowboys, completing 23 of 29 passes for 230 yards and three touchdowns while also rushing for 54 yards. 

Dart is expected to make a full recovery.

Dallas Mavericks center Dereck Lively II has not been cleared for training camp and his status for the start of the regular season has yet to be determined as he continues to recover from right foot surgery, sources told ESPN's Tim MacMahon.

After playing a key role as a rookie in the Mavericks' run to the 2024 NBA Finals, Lively's promising career has been derailed by recurring problems with his right foot, which has been surgically repaired twice in the last 14 months.

The sides have spent extensive time discussing a potential extension during the offseason, but there has been no movement lately in negotiations, sources said, as the Knicks stand to go for a repeat following their first NBA title in 53 years.

articles.headline: Man City refuse to deny guilty verdicts in Premier League 115 breaches case
articles.description: Manchester City on Friday did not deny there has been a guilty verdict in the majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.
articles.body:
Manchester City on Friday did not deny there has been a guilty verdict in the majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

Both the club and the Premier League have been approached by ESPN over media reports that City have been found guilty in 114 of 115 counts by an independent panel.

When contacted by ESPN on Friday, the Premier League said they wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

City also did not deny that they have been informed of the panel's decision and instead released a statement insisting that the process "remains ongoing."

One source has told ESPN that City sought an injunction Friday to block initial reporting of the verdict. City strongly denied that is the case when approached by ESPN.

It is expected that City -- which could face anything from a fine, points deduction or expulsion from the Premier League by way of punishment -- will appeal any guilty verdict.

A statement issued by City on Friday read: "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC's position remains consistent with the club's statement of February 2023.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

The Premier League announced the charges against City in February 2023 following a four-year investigation.

The case was heard at an independent hearing at the International Dispute Resolution Centre in London, beginning in September 2024. It came to an end in December 2024 after 12 weeks of deliberations.

The alleged breaches of financial rules were said to have occurred over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

The Premier League's claim was centered around their belief that City did not provide "accurate financial information that gives a true and fair view of the club's financial position."

City have maintained their innocence throughout the process.

In February 2020, City were found guilty of breaking UEFA's FFP rules and given a two-year ban from European competition and €30m fine.

The suspension was lifted by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) five months later with the fine reduced to €10m.

articles.headline: Cooper Flagg's rookie debut patch card sells for record $8.04 million
articles.description: The card was sold in early Friday morning at 2 a.m. ET.
articles.body:
Cooper Flagg's rookie season added yet another accolade -- and this time, it's historic.

Early Friday morning, Flagg's NBA rookie debut patch card sold for a whopping $8.04 million in Fanatics Collect's September Premier Auction. The card received 83 bids during the two-week auction.

According to Fanatics, a late bidding war took place for the card, and the price skyrocketed from $3.5 million at approximately 9 p.m. ET Thursday to $8.04 million at 2 a.m. ET Friday.

The sale set records for the most expensive basketball card sale featuring a single player and the most expensive debut patch sale, passing Pittsburgh Pirates pitcher Paul Skenes' debut patch record of $1.1 million.

It also is the third-most-expensive NBA card sale, trailing dual card sales of LeBron James-Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant-Jordan, Fanatics says.

In the same auction, two other debut patch cards sold for high amounts -- San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper's debut patch sold for $2.88 million, and Charlotte Hornets sharpshooter Kon Knueppel's sold for $2.34 million.

Flagg's card was pulled in a break by Rhody Breakers in Rhode Island and belonged to collector Jason Williams of South Carolina, according to Fanatics. He eventually put up the card for auction with Fanatics Collect.

The three cards rank among the most expensive debut patch sales of all time since the concept, which has expanded to leagues including the NFL and UEFA, was first introduced in MLB in 2023.

What adds a more historic spin to the sale is that this is the first class of NBA debut patch cards for which each rookie drafted in the 2025 class wore a patch in his first game that was removed at the game's conclusion, put into a card and signed by the player.

Flagg, 19, made his NBA debut with the Dallas Mavericks on Oct. 22, when he dropped 10 points and snatched 10 rebounds in a 125-92 loss against the Spurs.

articles.headline: LeBron James: Maxey friendship, helping Embiid were 76ers factors
articles.description: LeBron James says his long-standing friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign with the 76ers.
articles.body:
LeBron James said his long-standing friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

James, 41, revealed some details about the free agency process and what helped put the 76ers over the top on his "Mind the Game" podcast with co-host Steve Nash that dropped Friday.

"I think I'm more in love with the pursuit of how much more can I defy the odds," James said on the podcast.

James said "Philly was not even a question" early in his decision-making until the Sixers pulled the surprising deal with the Boston Celtics for NBA Finals MVP and champion Jaylen Brown. James and Maxey share an agent and have been friends and workout partners since the Sixers guard broke into the league, a friendship that turned into a recruiting pitch for the NBA's career scoring leader.

"When I became a free agent and we decided to let the Lakers know that I wouldn't be returning, he was one of the first people that was on my line, calling me," James said of Maxey.

James also was intrigued with trying to help oft-injured Embiid win his first title. Embiid has won an NBA MVP, two scoring titles and an Olympic gold medal but has yet to lead the Sixers beyond the second round of the playoffs since Philadelphia selected him third overall in the 2014 draft.

"He's done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into The Process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

The Sixers went 45-37 last season and were swept in the second round by the eventual NBA champion New York Knicks.

James praised Brown for bringing an unwavering voice and energy of his own.

"I just think any time someone moves to their own beat, it makes someone uncomfortable," James said of Brown. "He has his own voice. He moves to the sound of his own beat. It makes people uncomfortable because it's not what everyone is accustomed to."

James is scheduled to meet with reporters for the first time as a Sixer on Monday at the team's media day in Camden, New Jersey. Training camp opens next week.

A four-time NBA champion, James wrote on social media when he signed with the Sixers that he felt he was "done" when his 23rd NBA season ended, his last with the Lakers. But after time away with family, and still feeling physically and mentally strong in offseason workouts, James decided he wanted to keep playing.

James called it "humbling" to play for the Lakers and expressed disappointment that he wasn't able to enjoy a championship parade because of the 2020 pandemic. He called Los Angeles home and said it would be for "the foreseeable future."

articles.headline: Jets' No. 1 TE Mason Taylor (thumb) out vs. high-scoring Lions
articles.description: The Jets will be without No. 1 tight end Mason Taylor (thumb) and safety Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin) when they face the Detroit Lions on Sunday.
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- The New York Jets will face the high-scoring Detroit Lions on Sunday without No. 1 tight end Mason Taylor, who was ruled out Friday with a thumb injury.

Taylor, injured last Sunday against the Green Bay Packers, didn't practice all week and is considered week-to-week.

"[It] won't be long," coach Aaron Glenn said of Taylor's absence.

Taylor has only two receptions for minus-2 yards, but he has logged more snaps than any of the five tight ends on the roster. This should mean a bigger role for first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq, who has five catches for 38 yards and a rushing touchdown.

The Jets (1-1) are thin at wide receiver -- three players on injured reserve -- and now Adonai Mitchell is dealing with a finger injury. He was limited in practice on Friday. He got a finger caught in a jersey on Thursday, according to Glenn, who said, "I don't think he broke it."

Glenn wouldn't comment on Mitchell's availability for Sunday.

If Mitchell is limited by the injury, it leaves Garrett Wilson and Isaiah Williams as the only healthy receivers with NFL experience. They also have undrafted rookie Malik McClain, who was signed this week from the practice squad, primarily for special teams. Glenn said they will promote one of the veterans from the practice squad, either Sterling Shepard or Tyler Johnson.

As expected, safety Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin) will miss his second consecutive game. The secondary held up well last week against the Packers, limiting Jordan Love to 145 passing yards, but the Lions (1-1) represent a greater challenge.

"This will be one of the most explosive groups that we'll go against, to me, probably all year," said Glenn, calling Jared Goff "one of the most accurate quarterbacks I've ever been around." He was the Lions' defensive coordinator from 2021-24.

The Jets have gone an NFL-record 19 straight games without making an interception.

Edge rusher Joseph Ossai (foot) and rookie cornerback D'Angelo Ponds (calf) practiced fully on Friday and could make their Jets debuts on Sunday.
